speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help assess the newborn's increasing yellow discoloration, could you please tell me how old the infant is in days and whether the jaundice appeared within the first 24 hours of life? I also need to know if the baby is feeding well and having normal wet diapers.

speaker: Patient
text: 2-week-old female newborn. The patient has been experiencing increasing yellow discoloration of her eyes and skin for 2 days. She was born at 39 weeks' gestation, initially weighed 3066 g and now weighs 3200 g. The patient is exclusively breastfed.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you, the weight gain and exclusive breastfeeding are reassuring signs. Does the infant have any fever, poor feeding, or unusual sleepiness, and have you noticed if her stools have become pale or clay-colored?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Increasing yellow discoloration of the eyes and skin. I also have Exclusively breastfed, Brother died 3 months after liver surgery.

speaker: Doctor
text:

text: The laboratory results show predominantly unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia with normal liver enzymes and a negative Coombs test, which effectively rules out hemolytic disease of the newborn and biliary atresia.
